spots.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa
spots.summary: Jemaa el-Fnaa, also Jemaa el-Fna, Djema el-Fna or Djemaa el-Fnaa, is a square and market place in the medina quarter of Marrakesh, Morocco. It remains the main square of Marrakesh, used by locals and tourists.

spots.name: Majorelle Garden
spots.summary: The Majorelle Garden is a one-hectare (two-acre) botanical garden and artist's landscape garden in Marrakesh, Morocco. It was created by the French Orientalist artist Jacques Majorelle over almost forty years, starting in 1923, and features a Cubist villa designed by French architect Paul Sinoir in the 1930s.

spots.name: Kutubiyya Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kutubiyya Mosque or Koutoubia Mosque is the largest mosque in Marrakesh, Morocco. It is located in the southwest medina quarter of Marrakesh, near the Jemaa el-Fnaa market place, and is flanked by large gardens.

spots.name: Bahia Palace
spots.summary: The Bahia Palace is a mid to late 19th-century palace in Marrakesh, Morocco. The palace was first begun by Si Musa, grand vizier under the Alawi sultan Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, in the 1860s. It was expanded by his son Si Ba Ahmed ibn Musa, grand vizier of Sultan Moulay Abdelaziz, between 1894 and 1900.

spots.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
spots.summary: The Ben Youssef Madrasa is an Islamic madrasa (college) in Marrakesh, Morocco. The madrasa is named after the adjacent Ben Youssef Mosque, and was commissioned in 1564–65 CE by the Saadian sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib.

spots.name: El Badi Palace
spots.summary: El Badi Palace or Badi' Palace is a ruined palace in Marrakesh, Morocco. It was commissioned by the sultan Ahmad al-Mansur of the Saadian dynasty a few months after his accession in 1578, with construction and embellishment continuing throughout most of his reign.

spots.name: Saadian Tombs
spots.summary: The Saadian Tombs are a historic royal necropolis in Marrakesh, Morocco, located on the south side of the Kasbah Mosque, inside the royal kasbah (citadel) district of the city.

spots.name: Medina of Marrakesh
spots.summary: Marrakesh or Marrakech is the fourth-largest city in Morocco. It is one of the four imperial cities of Morocco and is the capital of the Marrakesh-Safi region. The city lies west of the foothills of the Atlas Mountains.

spots.name: Almoravid Qubba
spots.summary: The Almoravid Qubba, also known as the Qubbat al-Ba'diyyin or Qubbat al-Barudiyyin, is a small monument in Marrakesh, Morocco. It was erected by the Almoravid dynasty in the early 12th century. It is notable for its extraordinary decoration and for being one of the only remnants of Almoravid architecture in Marrakesh.

spots.name: Ben Youssef Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ben Youssef Mosque or Ibn Yusuf Mosque, is a mosque in the Medina quarter of Marrakesh, Morocco, named after the Almoravid ruler Ali ibn Yusuf. The mosque was originally founded in either the late 11th or early 12th century as the city's principal congregational mosque.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Marrakech Museum
spots.summary: The Museum of Marrakech is a historic palace and museum located in the old center of Marrakesh, Morocco. In addition to its notable architecture, the museum's collection showcases various historic art objects and contemporary art from Morocco.

spots.name: Bab Agnaou
spots.summary: Bab Agnaou, also transliterated as Bab Agnaw, is one of the best-known gates of Marrakesh, Morocco. Its construction is attributed to the Almohad caliph Abu Yusuf Ya'qub al-Mansur and was completed around 1188 or 1190.

spots.name: Yves Saint Laurent Museum in Marrakesh
spots.summary: The Yves Saint Laurent Museum in Marrakech is a museum dedicated to the fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent located in Marrakesh, Morocco.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Yves Saint Laurent Museum in Marrakesh

spots.name: Dar el Bacha
spots.summary: Dar el Bacha is a palace situated in the old medina of Marrakesh, Morocco. It currently houses the Museum of Confluences.

spots.name: Al-Mansour Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kasbah Mosque, also known as the Moulay al-Yazid Mosque, is a historic mosque in Marrakesh, Morocco. It was originally built by the Almohad ruler Yaqub al-Mansur in 1185–1190 CE. It is located in the Kasbah district, the city's former citadel, near the site of its historic royal palaces.

spots.name: Slat al-Azama Synagogue
spots.summary: The Slat al-Azama Synagogue or Lazama Synagogue is a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in Marrakesh, Marrakesh-Safi, Morocco. It is located in the historic Mellah of the old city.

photo.author: David Berkowitz from New York, NY, USA

spots.name: Walls of Marrakesh
spots.summary: The Walls of Marrakesh are a set of defensive ramparts which enclose the historic medina districts of Marrakesh, Morocco. They were first laid out in the early 12th century by the Almoravid dynasty which founded the city in 1070 CE as their new capital.

spots.name: Dar Si Said
spots.summary: Dar Si Said is a historic late 19th-century palace and present-day museum in Marrakesh, Morocco. It currently houses the National Museum of Weaving and Carpets.

spots.name: Mouassine Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mouassine Mosque or al-Muwassin Mosque is a major mosque in the Mouassine neighbourhood of Marrakesh, Morocco. It was built in the 16th century by order of the Saadian sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib.

spots.name: Bab Doukkala
spots.summary: Bab Doukkala is the main northwestern gate of the medina of Marrakesh, Morocco.

spots.name: Zawiya of Sidi Bel Abbes
spots.summary: The Zawiya of Sidi Bel Abbes is a zawiya in Marrakesh, Morocco. The complex is centered around the mausoleum of Abu al-Abbas al-Sabti, a Sufi teacher who died in 1204. He is the most venerated of the Seven Saints of Marrakesh, generally considered the "patron saint" of the city.

spots.name: Mosque of the Cat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mosque of the Cat is a historic mosque in Marrakesh, Morocco. It is also identified in some scholarly sources as the Moulay al-Ksour Mosque or Mawlā al-Qṣūr Mosque.

spots.name: Mouassine Museum
spots.summary: The Mouassine Museum is a museum in the Mouassine neighbourhood of the historic medina of Marrakesh, Morocco. The museum is housed in a recently restored 16th to 17th-century house which includes an upper-floor apartment known as a douiria.

spots.name: Mouassine Fountain
spots.summary: The Mouassine Fountain is a part of the 16th-century religious complex of the Mouassine Mosque in Marrakesh, Morocco. The tradition of building public fountains in Marrakesh is old but took on a very monumental character in the Saadian era.

spots.name: Bab er Robb
spots.summary: Bab er Robb is a southern city gate in the historic medina of Marrakesh, Morocco.

spots.name: Bab ad-Debbagh
spots.summary: Bab ad-Debbagh or Bab Debbagh is one of the main eastern gates of the medina of Marrakesh, Morocco.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A little photography museum, it has one of the highest roof terraces in the Medina. Ticket is also valid for Museum of Mouassin Music.

spots.name: The Souks
spots.summary: Markets of Marrakech, just adjacent to Place Djemaa El-Fna, are where you can buy almost anything, from spices to shoes, jellabas to kaftans, and tea pots to tagines. Undoubtedly, being a foreigner means you will end up paying higher prices than a native would, but be sure to bargain nonetheless. spots.name: Moroccan Culinary Arts Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: If you are interested in food and eating culture, you will enjoy this museum. Audiovisual information about the rich culinary culture of Marocco, its ingredients, techniques and traditions. You can also touch and smell many things. They also sport a very well equipped cooking school.
